([[Mouth of Wilson, Virginia]]) | college = [[Duke Blue Devils men's basketball|Duke]] (2016–2017) | draft_year = | draft_round = | draft_pick = | draft_team = | career_start = | years1 = | team1 = | highlights = * [[Jordan Brand Classic]] (2016) * [[Nike Hoop Summit]] (2016) | medal_templates = {{MedalCountry|the {{USA}}}} {{MedalCompetition|[[FIBA Under-19 World Championship|FIBA World U19 Championship]]}} {{MedalGold| [[2015 FIBA Under-19 World Championship|2015 Greece]] | [[United States men's national under-19 basketball team|National team]]}} {{MedalCompetition|[[FIBA Americas Under-16 Championship|FIBA Americas U16 Championship]]}} {{MedalGold| [[FIBA Americas Under-16 Championship|2013 Uruguay]] | [[United States men's national under-17 basketball team|National team]]}} }} '''Harry Lee Giles III''' (born April 22, 1998) is an American [[basketball]] player. He played college basketball at [[Duke Blue Devils men's basketball|Duke University]]. Giles became a five-star recruit and was generally seen as the best overall recruit in the 2016 Class by most basketball recruiting services. On November 6, 2015, Harry announced his intentions to attend and play for [[Duke University]]. ==Early life== Giles was born April 22, 1998 in [[Winston-Salem, North Carolina]] to parents Harry Giles Sr and Melissa Addison Giles. His father played both basketball and football for [[Winston-Salem State University]]. ==High school career== Giles attended the [[Wesleyan Christian Academy]] in [[High Point, North Carolina]] from his Freshman to Junior year. As a freshman, Giles averaged 12.5 [[points per game]] and 9.5 [[rebounds per game]] after leading Wesleyan Christian to a 2013 NCISAA 3A State Championship alongside current UNC shooting guard [[Theo Pinson]]. Giles missed his entire sophomore year due to a left knee injury.{{Cite news|url=http://www.greensboro.com/harry-giles-will-miss-sophomore-season-after-knee-surgery/article_749ec98e-f4ac-11e2-bf29-0019bb30f31a.html|title=Harry Giles will miss sophomore season after knee surgery|last=Reynolds|first=David|date=July 24, 2013|work=Www.greensboro.com|access-date=April 16, 2017|archive-url=|archive-date=|dead-url=}} during the 2014 summer, Giles participated in the [[Under Armour]] Elite 24 game in [[Brooklyn, New York]] where he earned Co-MVP honors alongside Chase Jeter. After shining for his AAU team, CP3 All-Stars in 2014, the 6-foot-9 power forward entered his junior year hungrier and more focused than ever to reclaim his spot as the #1 player in the Class of 2016. In his junior year, Giles and Wesleyan was ranked #2 team in the country by USA Today. On November 14, 2014 In his second game back since his injury, Harry scored a career high 38 points and grabbed 19 rebounds in a (82-58) win over [[Northside Christian Academy]]. Giles and the Trojans then played in the 2014-15 High School OT Holiday Invitational Tournament at [[Needham B. Broughton High School]] in [[Raleigh, North Carolina]]. On December 29, Giles and Wesleyan defeated [[Word of God Christian Academy]] (98-85) behind Giles 31 points and 17 rebounds to advance to the championship game.{{Cite news|url=http://www.highschoolot.com/wesleyan-hands-word-of-god-first-loss-moves-on-to-championship/14315807/|title=Wesleyan hands word of God its first loss move on to Championship|last=Smith III|first=Junious|date=December 30, 2014|work=Www.highschoolot.com|access-date=May 22, 2017|archive-url=|archive-date=|dead-url=}} On December 30th, Giles went head to head against an [[Orangeville Prep]] team that featured former #1 player in 2016 [[Thon Maker]]. The Wesleyan trojans would defeat Orangeville Prep (78-75) with Giles scoring 26 points and 14 rebounds while Maker scored 24 points and 11 between the two.{{Cite news|url=http://www.fayobserver.com/article/20141230/Blogs/312309752|title=Harry Giles and Wesleyan defeat thon Maker and Orangeville Prep|last=Strelow|first=Brett|date=December 30, 2014|work=Www.fayobserver.com|access-date=May 22, 2017|archive-url=|archive-date=|dead-url=}} On January 15, 2015, Giles scored 17 points, 12 rebounds, and 4 Assist to help the Trojans defeat [[Bentonville High School]] (63-55) on the first day of the Bass Pro Tournament of Champions Tournament who were led by [[Malik Monk]]. On the season Giles averaged 23.9 [[points per game]],12.5 [[rebounds per game]], 2.0 assist per game, and 2.0 blocks per game while leading the Wesleyan Trojans to a (30-5) record and a NCISAA 3A state championship game appearance unfortunately losing to in state rival [[Greensboro Day School]]. Giles would soon rejoin his [[Amateur Athletic Union|AAU]] Team CP3 All Stars, sponsored by fellow [[Winston-Salem]] native and NBA superstar [[Chris Paul]] of the [[Los Angeles Clippers]].{{cite web| last = | first = | title = Harry Giles, top NC high school basketball player, will transfer to Oak Hill Academy | publisher = CharlotteObserver.com | date = Jul 30, 2015 | url = http://www.charlotteobserver.com/sports/college/mens-basketball/article29575141.html | access-date = August 29, 2015}} Harry led the Team CP3 All Stars to the 2015 Nike Elite Youth Basketball League (EYBL) Peach Jam semifinals against the St. Louis Eagles featuring future Duke teammate [[Jayson Tatum]]. Unfortunately Team CP3 would lose by a game winning buzzer beater. He averaged 18.2 [[points per game]] and 12.0 [[rebounds per game]] in 16 games on the EYBL circuit. Before his senior season, Giles decided to attend and play for the high school basketball powerhouse [[Oak Hill Academy (Mouth of Wilson, Virginia)|Oak Hill Academy]] in [[Mouth of Wilson, Virginia]]. Giles dominated the majority of his high school career; however, his senior year ended with a very serious injury.http://www.dukebasketballreport.com/2016/8/12/12449926/harry-giles-is-working-hard-in-rehab The injury occurred during his first scrimmage game with Oak Hill Academy. Weeks later, Giles enrolled to (now defunct) Forest Trail Academy in [[Kernersville, North Carolina]] to take online courses to finish his senior year of high school while rehabbing his knee injury. He was selected to play in the 2016 [[Jordan Brand Classic]] and [[Nike Hoop Summit]] but was unable due to injury.{{Cite news|url=http://usatodayhss.com/2016/harry-giles-iii-excited-to-be-a-part-of-a-postseason-all-star-game-jordan-brand-classic|title=Harry Giles excited to be a part of a postseason all star game Jordan Brand Classic|last=Jordan|first=Jason|date=April 14, 2016|work=Www.usatodayhss.com|access-date=April 16, 2017|archive-url=|archive-date=|dead-url=}}{{Cite news|url=http://usatodayhss.com/2016/harry-giles-iii-in-no-rush-to-get-back-on-the-court-focused-on-fun-at-nike-hoop-summit-duke-jayson-tatum|title=Harry Giles in no rush to get back on the court focused on fun at Nike hoop summit|last=Jordan|first=Jason|date=April 9, 2016|work=Www.usatodayhss.com|access-date=April 16, 2017|archive-url=|archive-date=|dead-url=}} Giles was rated as a five-star recruit and ranked the No.1 overall player in the 2016 high school class by [[ESPN]], while [[Scout.com]] and [[Rivals.com|Rivals]] ranked him No. 2 in the Class of 2016 only behind [[Josh Jackson (basketball)|Josh Jackson]].{{Cite news|url=http://usatodayhss.com/2016/harry-giles-finishes-no-1-josh-jackson-up-to-no-2-in-final-espn-100-for-class-of-2016|title=Harry Giles finishes as No.1 player in Espn 100 For 2016, Jackson is No. 2|last=|first=|date=April 26, 2016|work=Www.usatodayhss.com|access-date=May 22, 2016|archive-url=|archive-date=|dead-url=}} ==College career== ===Duke (2016–2017)=== Giles was originally recruited by [[Wake Forest University]], [[Duke University]], [[University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill|University of North Carolina]], [[University of Kentucky]] and [[University of Kansas]]. On November 6, 2015 Giles committed to [[Duke University]].{{Cite news|url=https://www.si.com/college-basketball/2015/11/06/harry-giles-recruiting-commit-duke-coach-k|title=2016 No. 1 recruit Harry Giles Commits to Duke|last=Johnson|first=Chris|date=November 6, 2015|work=Www.si.com|access-date=April 25, 2017|archive-url=|archive-date=|dead-url=}} On October 3, 2016 it was announced Giles would likely miss up to six weeks to have surgery on his knee. On December 19, 2016, Giles made his college debut against [[Tennessee State Tigers basketball|Tennessee State]], playing for four minutes. On March 10, 2017 in a game against rival UNC, Giles had four blocks.{{Cite news|url=http://www.dukechronicle.com/article/2017/03/harry-giles-shines-in-dukes-acc-tournament-upset-of-top-seeded-north-carolina|title=Harry Giles shines in duke's ACC tournament upset of top seeded North Carolina|last=Tucker|first=Hank|date=March 11, 2017|work=Www.dukechronicle.com|access-date=April 16, 2017|archive-url=|archive-date=|dead-url=}} At the conclusion of his freshman season, Giles announced that he would forgo his final three years of collegiate eligibility and enter the [[2017 NBA draft]].{{cite web|url=http://www.cbssports.com/college-basketball/news/dukes-harry-giles-entering-nba-draft-despite-disappointing-freshman-season/|title=Duke’s Harry Giles entering NBA Draft despite disappointing freshman season|website=cbssports.com|author=Gary Parrish|date=2017-03-28|accessdate=2017-03-28}} ===College statistics=== {{NBA player statistics start}} |- | style="text-align:left;"| [[2016–17 NCAA Division I men's basketball season|2016–17]] | style="text-align:left;"| [[2016–17 Duke Blue Devils men's basketball team|Duke]] | 26 || 6 || 11.5 || .577 || .000 || .500 || 3.9 || .4 || .4 || .7 || 3.9 {{S-end}} ==International career== Harry Giles competed for [[United States men's national basketball team|Team USA]] in the 2015 FIBA Under-19 World Championship in [[Greece]]. In the tournament he finished third in points per game per 40 minutes with 26.4, second in offensive board percentage with 17.1%, and first in defensive rebounding percentage with 28.7%.{{cite web| last =Winn | first =Luke | title = Jalen Brunson, Harry Giles star as USA wins FIBA U19 World Championship | publisher = SportsIllustrated.com | date = Jul 6, 2015 | url = http://www.si.com/college-basketball/2015/07/06/fiba-u19-world-championship-usa-jalen-brunson-harry-giles | accessdate = August 29, 2015}} ==References== {{Reflist}} ==External links== *[http://www.goduke.com/ViewArticle.dbml?ATCLID=211021387&DB_OEM_ID=4200 Duke Blue Devils bio] {{DEFAULTSORT:Giles, Harry}} [[Category:1998 births]] [[Category:Living people]] [[Category:Basketball players from North Carolina]] [[Category:Duke Blue Devils men's basketball players]] [[Category:Power forwards (basketball)]] [[Category:Sportspeople from Winston-Salem, North Carolina]]
